approval_time_estimate: Review required for public connections (timeline not published)
summary: Notion has two kinds of connections (formerly 'integrations'). Internal ones use a static token for one workspace and involve no OAuth. Public ones use OAuth 2.0 and can be installed in any workspace; their authorization URL only becomes available after the public connection is submitted for review. Users choose which pages to share, so your connection only sees what each user grants.
key_facts: Internal integrations are instant — no review needed (but only work in your own workspace)
Public connections use OAuth 2.0; the authorization URL is only issued after the connection is submitted for review (Notion publishes no review timeline)
Notion uses a unique permission model: users select specific pages to grant access, not entire workspaces
Your integration will NOT automatically see all user content — users must explicitly share pages
The installation scope (any workspace vs selected workspaces) cannot be changed after the connection is created
Token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth with your client ID and secret; store the refresh token to renew access
Composio managed auth available for prototyping

steps.title: Create a Notion Integration
steps.description: Go to notion.so/my-integrations and click '+ New integration'. Choose between Internal (your workspace only, instant) or Public (any user, requires review). Enter integration name and select the associated workspace.
warnings: Start with Internal type for development — switch to Public only when ready to submit for review

steps.title: Configure Integration Capabilities
steps.description: Set the content capabilities your integration needs: Read content, Update content, Insert content. Set User information access level. These become the permissions shown to users during OAuth.
warnings: Request only the capabilities you genuinely need — Notion reviewers check for over-permissioning

steps.title: Configure OAuth Settings (Public integrations)
steps.description: In the OAuth Domain & URIs section, add your redirect URIs. For Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Add your integration's company/website information for the authorization screen.

steps.title: Build and Test Your Integration
steps.description: Use the Internal Secret (API key) from your integration page for development testing. Share specific test pages with your integration to verify it can read/write content correctly.
warnings: Remember: even in production, users must explicitly share pages — build UX that guides them through this

steps.title: Submit Public Integration for Review
steps.description: Once your integration is ready, switch to Public type and fill in all required fields: integration URL, privacy policy URL, support email, tagline, description, screenshots. Then submit for Notion's review.
warnings: Integration URL must be a live, public page explaining what your integration does
Screenshots must show real usage of your integration

requirements.account_type: Free Notion account works for internal integrations; any account works for public

blockers.title: User Must Manually Share Pages
blockers.description: Notion's permission model means users grant access at the page/database level, not the workspace level. Your users will need to explicitly share each relevant page or database with your integration. This is unintuitive and a common source of user confusion.
blockers.workaround: Build clear UX with a setup checklist that walks users through sharing the right pages. Show screenshots/video of the sharing process.

blockers.title: Integration URL Required
blockers.description: Public integration review requires a live website URL for your integration. Placeholder pages or localhost URLs will cause rejection.
blockers.workaround: Deploy a simple landing page describing your integration before submitting for review.

if_blocked.situation: Authorization URL not shown for your public connection
if_blocked.action: Submit the connection for review in the developer portal; the URL is issued after submission.

if_blocked.situation: Your app cannot see a page
if_blocked.action: The user must share that page (or its parent) with the connection during authorization.
